summary: Slice E0 of 0.8.7 (the turn contract) is built in the worktree, uncommitted, and saved as a patch. New: workbench/turns.py, with the frozen interface written plainly at its top: TurnKind and Caps, the registry (register, kind_of, checker_modules, and discover, which finds kind-registering modules by reading the sources), layout() (the four-message contract: brief | stable | 'Ready.' | last), ask(kind, inputs, request) (switch and per-request ceiling, layout, grammar, tokens, price, deadline, the call, parse, check, one brain.turn/1 record, then the checked desk object or the fallback), Verdict, Fallback, Answer, TurnRequest (3 foreground turns, a 25 s budget, one question card), LocalPort (the only caller of local_brain.completion), FixedClock (used until brain_clock.py exists; guarded import), the brain.turn/1 ledger (its own table brain_turns, bounded to 30 days or 2,000 turns, tombstone on forget) and the read operations brain.turns and brain.turn.get. Also new: workbench/model_words.py (ModelSaid: str/format/f-string/%/+/iteration/in/json all raise, repr holds no words; Marked and marked() with the five mark lines; plain_only(); Invalid; strict terse-line parsers), workbench/grammars.py (a minimal GBNF builder with no free whitespace), and workbench/fake_worker.py (FakeWorker, an in-process port with virtual time and stand-in prompt reuse; FakeServer, a loopback HTTP stand-in for llama-server's five endpoints; FAKE, an example kind). Changed: local_brain.completion gains keyword-only grammar, timeout, t_max_predict_ms, odds and prompt_tokens (the positional API and the ready probes are unchanged, cache_prompt is still false); shell2.leaded and shell2.Bubble.set_text (her column's plain renderer) refuse model words; the Kernel and CLI registrations are in their own commented blocks; the registry record was regenerated on a copy and copied back. The only direct callers of local_brain.completion were the three ready probes in run_model_job, which are excepted, so no caller had to move. The smoke script printed 25 of 25 OK on two runs on throwaway copies, and the patch applies to a clean export of HEAD. Nothing was tested in the owner's sense, no model was loaded, and nothing ran on the ThinkPad.

decisions: parse takes (said, inputs), not just the text: a parser needs the option count to range-check. said is a ModelSaid and is read only through for_check().

Fallback codes: the five in design 3.5 (ASK_OWNER, DEFAULT_READ, PLAIN_WORDS, CANNOT_TELL, NOT_OFFERED), plus PATTERNS (MARKS' pattern pass) and PLACES (ASK's places list). Design 4.7 names those two no-model answers, and the five codes do not cover them.

Outcomes: the design's TAKEN, TRIMMED, REFUSED, LATE and TRIPPED, plus UNSETTLED and FAILED. UNSETTLED is the checker state from 3.2; its value goes back to the caller to make the one question. FAILED covers a worker error or no answer and is recorded. A turn that is not sent (switch off, AI off, no model, stopped, ceiling, over cap, over context) returns NOT_SENT with a reason and writes no record, because nothing went to the model.

brain.turn/1 is kept in its own Kernel table, brain_turns, not in desk_records. That keeps it local, off the Field and out of every receipt bundle. It is bounded to 30 days or 2,000 turns per owner, pruned at each write, and a digest is checked on read.

Only the read operations brain.turns and brain.turn.get are registered now. The Forget operation (approve scope, always asked) needs a stacy_hand ALWAYS_ASKS row, which is lane B's file, and the worker restart is A2's; both come later with brain.account and brain.help.set. The function turns.forget() (the tombstone) is there.

Switch defaults: understanding, choosing, reading pages and talk are on; wording is off (open question 3's default: live wording off). They are read from settings key brain.help, which brain.help.set will write.

Price and deadline are integer milliseconds: price = desk share + ceil(new x 1000 / read rate) + ceil(answer cap x 1000 / write rate). The deadline is min(kind cap, max(3000, 2 x price + 1000)), also capped by the request's remaining budget; a turn whose price exceeds what is left, or with under 3 s left, is not sent. FixedClock uses 30 tokens a second at 256 new tokens or fewer, 70 above, and writes at 5, the 4B's quiet rates rounded down. The default request budget is 25 s (the 4B here).

Until A2 turns prompt reuse on, every token of a question counts as new (LocalPort.kept() is 0). A kind whose brief is long, such as READ at up to 700 tokens against a 250 new-token cap, is therefore OVER_CAP on the real worker until then. The fake worker simulates reuse, so lane smoke scripts can exercise it.

Every kind except TALK and other Stop-only kinds must send a grammar, and a grammar with free whitespace is refused. I started grammars.py (one_of, choice, picks, check, admits) so the fake kind sends a real grammar; A3 owns and grows it.

Message text must be str, so model words (ModelSaid) can never be put back into a prompt as if the desk had written them. A brief that changes between calls is refused (TURN_BRIEF_CHANGED), because its sha256 is part of the kind.
A parser or checker that crashes refuses the answer (fails closed) and is recorded. ask() raises only for a kind that breaks the contract.
The eleven known kind names are bound to their switches (SWITCH_OF), so a lane cannot register NEXT under 'understanding'. Other upper-case names are allowed for exam shapes and stand-ins.
fake_worker.py lives in workbench/ so later smoke scripts can import it. It is never wired into the app, and FAKE is registered only by register_fake().

release_note: 0.8.7 starts with one door for every question Kas puts to a local model. Each kind of question is registered once, priced and given a deadline before it is sent. Its answer comes back as a short checked shape, and it is written to a private turn ledger on this computer that you can read. Anything the model writes is held as the model's own words: it cannot be shown as hers, and a change only the model chose is refused. With no model, or with a kind switched off, she answers exactly as she does without one. It was built under the no-tests rule and has not been tested, and no model was run for it.
